Full summary: Stage 3 (D3): staleness probes fixed — compound-scope splitting, git-mv basename fallback, capped scores with noisy-or; plus twining_unarchive, archive_stale batch warning, and archived_excluded_count in assemble/why
Decisions: Chose noisy-or aggregation over keeping max() with lowered caps — max() means independent signals can never corroborate, so capping every heuristic below threshold would have made staleness_review return nothing; noisy-or lets scope 0.8 + files + branch 0.4 legitimately cross 0.95 while no single heuristic reaches certainty; Chose a git ls-files basename index over git log --follow for moved-file detection — one cheap subprocess per audit versus a per-missing-file history walk; the basename set covers the archive/-convention class that produced all six sampled field false positives; Chose a non-blocking batch-size warning on twining_archive_stale over a hard re-score gate — the semantic-review skill archives on LLM judgment the server cannot score, and forcing it through force:true would habituate overrides (user-confirmed fork); Chose to cap affected_files_missing at 0.95 rather than leaving proportion uncapped — an existsSync+basename miss is still a heuristic; 0.95 still crosses the default threshold alone when every file is gone, but certainty (1.0) is now unreachable by construction everywhere
Findings: The old staleness unit tests LOCKED IN the defective 1.0 scores — rewritten; the dashboard /health fixture also needed corroboration since a lone dead-scope no longer flags; warning: full-suite runs raced each other when backgrounded twice — two concurrent vitest invocations on this repo produce timeout/lock artifacts (plugin-bundle boots, golden fixture on live .twining/); never overlap suite runs; Verified the earlier 9 test failures were contention artifacts: same files pass 74/74 in 15s standalone
